narrative: Demand for PL1__M90CD9A1 is smooth and normally distributed at ~16,546 units/day with CV=16%, making a classical (r,Q) policy the natural fit. Lead times are moderate in mean (2.51 days) but variable (CV=50%), which drives a safety stock of 34,968 units to achieve the 95% service level. The EOQ of 166,044 units is well above the MOQ of 60,793, consolidating orders to ~25/year and reducing total annual inventory costs by 21.8% vs the SAP baseline. The SAP safety lead time of 4.5 days is overstated by ~2.4 days relative to the data-derived recommendation of 2.07 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth, continuous, and normally distributed (CV=16%, zero intermittency). The (r,Q) model with Normal-approximation safety stock is analytically exact for this regime, operationally simple to configure in SAP (MRP type VB or reorder-point planning), and delivers the global cost minimum via EOQ.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage utilisation after replenishment is 65.5% (201,012 of 306,772 units), leaving 105,760 units of headroom. No capacity-driven order reduction was required. If demand grows >15%, the post-replenishment stock level should be re-validated against the storage limit.
